heading: Book II.
paragraphs: Argument--In this book Augustin reviews those calamities which the Romans suffered before the time of Christ, and while the worship of the false gods was universally practised; and demonstrates that, far from being preserved from misfortune by the gods, the Romans have been by them overwhelmed with the only, or at least the greatest, of all calamities--the corruption of manners, and the vices of the soul. __________________________________________________________________
